name: TX-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by twelve points and the national environment favors GOP House candidates
Fallon holds a roughly 50-to-1 fundraising edge, with about $1.1 million on hand versus $2,000 for Pearce
Prediction markets price a Fallon win at about 96 percent
No polls or expert ratings flag any incumbent vulnerability
model.rationale: The district's twelve-point Republican lean, Fallon's overwhelming cash advantage, and markets pricing his win near 96 percent leave Pearce without a visible path, and no polling or ratings suggest the incumbent is vulnerable.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending backing Pearce or a surprise poll showing a single-digit race would be the main signal to revisit this rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's 4th District, a Republican-leaning seat in northeast Texas, features incumbent Pat Fallon seeking re-election against Democrat Jason Pearce. No public polls or expert ratings track the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, campaign finance, and prediction markets, all of which point toward the incumbent.

Fallon has raised about $790,000 and holds roughly $1.1 million on hand, while Pearce has raised about $16,000 with roughly $2,000 available, leaving the challenger little capacity to reach voters. Prediction markets price a Fallon win at about 96 percent. The district's twelve-point Republican lean, combined with an environment favoring Republican House candidates, makes an upset unlikely, and the race is rated Safe Republican.
